lead.headline: Stocks rise 15.0 to 273.5 in three hours; Exchange closed today and tomorrow
lead.deck: 7,150,000 shares between noon and 3 p.m.; ticker on time at the close; brokers' clerks to work both days on the accounts; Queens Exchange to keep 40 positions for brokers' calls
lead.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday in a session of three hours on a volume of 7,150,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 273.5, a gain of 15.0, the Exchange states. The ticker ran on time at the close. The tone book enters 'up.' The Exchange is closed today and tomorrow for the clearing of accounts, and brokers' offices state that their clerks will work through both days. The Queens Exchange will keep 40 positions for brokers' calls, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states.

columns.headline: Hallowe'en complaints in Queens put at 188; 31 concern removed gates
columns.body: The Police Department states that 188 complaints were made in Queens precincts last night, against 212 last year, 31 of them concerning removed gates and 64 soaped windows. Eleven were heard against the house record and dismissed. A gate in Sunnyside, wired shut, was not removed.

columns.headline: Mr. Ewald to deposit the Arcade's November rent with the clerk at 10 a.m.
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald states that he will deposit the Vantry Arcade's November rent of 412 dollars with the clerk of the Municipal Court at 10 a.m. today, the sixth month so deposited. The clerk will then hold 2,472 dollars for Signal Ground Rents Inc.

columns.headline: Hut cat at Port Washington faces the door at 2 a.m. for a twentieth night
columns.body: Mr. Silas Brewer, harbour master at Port Washington, states that the cat kept in the hut lent to the Radio Division turned from the Sound at 2 a.m. today for the twentieth night and faced the hut's door until 4 a.m. A saucer left by the door was not touched.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Queens Exchange states 618 calls reporting the tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. today, the operators entering 'louder.'

speaker.ear: Cooler. High 52. Friday. No market today. Count your fingers instead.

lead.headline: Ewald's rent goes in at ten, and the landlord still won't pick up
lead.deck: Eleven shops paid in the week of all weeks, the court clerk's drawer now holds two thousand four hundred and seventy-two dollars, and Signal Ground Rents sends nobody
lead.body: At ten this morning Mr. Ewald walked into the Municipal Court with the Arcade's November rent, four hundred and twelve dollars, every shop paid, in the week when half of Queens could not pay its broker. The clerk counted it twice and put it in the second drawer with the rest. That makes two thousand four hundred and seventy-two dollars waiting for a landlord who empties a post box and answers no telephone. Mr. Ewald asked whether anybody had called. The clerk said, 'Not a soul.'

columns.headline: Party Line's thirty-first Friday, and the parcel window is left on hold
columns.body: Thirty-one Fridays without a tin from Corona. Party Line passed the parcel window at four today, did not look, and went to Position 12. The night girl, who put through four hundred margin calls last week, says the cat is the only one at the board who sleeps.

columns.headline: Hallowe'en: Queens soaps its windows, and the house records play it back
columns.body: A hundred and eighty-eight complaints, which the Police call a quiet night. Eleven householders had the soaping played back against the house record and found the soaper was their own child. The Sunnyside man's wired gate held. He is leaving the wire on till Christmas.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'The market is shut. Why does my broker still ring?'
columns.body: Sir, because the market is shut and his clerks are not. He is adding up what you owe him while it holds still. The operator will put him through, and she will not hurry him. You may ask her the time. That, at least, is free.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Broad Street, nine o'clock: every broker's office lit, the Exchange dark. A clerk on a stoop said the figures would not add up, and went back in to add them.

record.ear: Fair. High 49. Low 36. First frost at Jamaica.

lead.headline: Week's count: 21,640 margin calls placed to Queens; 7,310 read by operators
lead.deck: Queens Exchange's figures for the seven days to Friday; brokers' calls fall to 1,900 yesterday with the Stock Exchange closed; tone calls 3,290, 'louder' on the five nights taken
lead.body: The Queens Exchange placed 21,640 calls from brokers to Queens subscribers in the seven days to Friday asking for margin, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the operators reading 7,310 brokers' messages where the broker could not hold. Yesterday, the Stock Exchange being closed, such calls fell to 1,900. The Exchange logged 3,290 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the week reporting the tone, entered 'louder' on the five nights taken. Queens Light & Power made no statement.

columns.headline: Municipal Court clerk receives the Arcade's November rent; holds 2,472 dollars
columns.body: The clerk of the Municipal Court states that he received 412 dollars from Mr. Nathan Ewald at 10:04 a.m. yesterday, the Vantry Arcade's November rent, and now holds 2,472 dollars for Signal Ground Rents Inc. He has written to the company's box at the General Post Office.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a thirty-first Friday
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the thirty-first Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal passed the parcel window at 4 p.m. without stopping and remained at Position 12 until the morning shift.

columns.headline: Valves at a dollar forty the six; Flushing dealers keep sales to one box
columns.body: The Queens Radio Dealers' Association states that valves held at a dollar forty the six this week, dealers in Flushing and Jamaica keeping sales to one box a customer. Eggs were 53 cents. The Newark works state that night shifts began on Monday.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Frost. High 49. Saturday. No market. Valves the only thing going up.

lead.headline: Valves at a dollar forty: Queens pays top dollar to hear the bottom fall out
lead.deck: One box to a customer in Flushing, a queue at the Arcade before eight, and the reason given at every counter is the same: they want to hear it before the paper does
lead.body: News & Cigars at the Arcade had a queue at ten to eight this morning, and it was not for the Speaker. It was for valves, one box to a customer, a dollar forty the six. A Corona man said he wanted his set warm before the brokers rang. A Woodhaven widow said she had no shares and wanted to hear who did. The Newark works are on night shifts. The Speaker would only point out that bad news on a cold set is free.

columns.headline: Twenty-one thousand margin calls, and the operators put a kind word through
columns.body: In the week to Friday the Queens Exchange put through twenty-one thousand six hundred calls from brokers asking for money, and the girls read seven thousand three hundred of the messages into kitchens themselves. Mr. Arne says they read exactly. The kitchens say they read kindly. Both may be true.

columns.headline: The Hum works the night shift, and the light company stays off the line
columns.body: Three thousand two hundred and ninety calls about the night tone this week, 'louder' every night the girls had time to write it down. Dr. Rastin says his needle has not had a night off since September. Queens Light & Power has had seven.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: Forest Hills deals again, and the brokers are told to hold
columns.body: Darlings, the Forest Hills bridge club met again on Wednesday, by telephone, the husbands having been forbidden the party line after six. Mrs. Ormsby bid four hearts. The Listening Lady could not hear the rest for a broker trying to get through, who was told firmly to hold.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Port Washington, two o'clock: Mr. Brewer's cat at the hut door for the twenty-first night. He says she has started sitting nearer.

lead.headline: Queens savings banks report deposits above withdrawals for the week
lead.deck: Fourteen member banks keep full hours; Corona Mutual states more callers than in any week since its founding; Christmas club payments unchanged; no bank asks notice of withdrawal
lead.body: The Savings Banks Association of Queens states that deposits at its 14 member banks exceeded withdrawals by 381,000 dollars in the week to Friday, and that no bank required notice of withdrawal. The Corona Mutual Savings Bank states that it received more callers in the week than in any since its founding in 1887, most of whom 'asked to see the book and went away.' Christmas club payments were unchanged. The Association's telephone was answered by its president on Thursday and Friday.

columns.headline: Stock Exchange to reopen at 10 a.m. tomorrow for a three-hour session
columns.body: The Stock Exchange will reopen at 10 a.m. tomorrow and close at 1 p.m., the governors state, and will keep three-hour sessions 'until the accounts are clear.' The Exchange will be closed on Tuesday, Election Day. The ticker was tested yesterday and found on time.

columns.headline: Byrd's geological party ready to leave Little America for the mountains
columns.body: Commander Richard E. Byrd states by wire that Dr. Laurence Gould's geological party will leave Little America with dog teams 'on the first fair day,' to lay depots for the polar flight. The temperature at the base on Friday was 9 below zero. The message concerned sledges.

columns.headline: Thirty-one churches to record sermons again after a week's interval
columns.body: The Queens Federation of Churches states that the 31 churches which switched off their house systems on October 27 will record this morning's sermons in the ordinary way, the congregations having so requested. The Federation states that last Sunday's sermons 'were heard once, as intended.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Queens Exchange states 641 calls reporting the tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. today, the operators entering 'louder.'

speaker.ear: Cold. High 46. Sunday. The banks are shut, and still standing.

lead.headline: Queens checks its balance, and finds it can still stand up
lead.deck: In Corona, Woodhaven and Long Island City the bank book comes out after supper; the savings banks took more callers this week than in forty years, and most only wanted a look
lead.body: This week in Queens the bank book came down off the mantel and onto the kitchen table, and families who own no stock at all sat down to count. The savings banks say they took in more than they paid out, and the Corona Mutual says most callers only asked to see their book and went home. A Woodhaven grandmother came twice, to be sure. The Speaker has no shares and one bank book, and has counted it. It came to the same both times.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Whitestone's porch set stays tuned, and Mr. Pike stays put
columns.body: The Whitestone man who heard WORS 1610 last Wednesday has sat up on his porch every night since, in an overcoat. Nothing. Mr. Pike says the report is still 'noted,' which is a drawer. The office boy's pin is still in the window frame.

columns.headline: Mr. Haskin signs 'for the property,' and the property isn't taking calls
columns.body: Nine days since somebody signed for Mr. Crane's letter at Buffalo as 'R. Haskin, for the property.' No reply. Mr. Crane has asked the Buffalo postmaster to describe the signer. The postmaster says tall, or else the counter is low, and that he has since had the counter raised.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can you tell me what my neighbours owe?'
columns.body: Madam, no, and she would not if she could, though she could. The girls on the Queens board heard more about your street this week than your street knows itself. They have agreed among themselves to forget it by Christmas. Ring your neighbour and ask her to supper.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Jackson Avenue, Sunday evening: the Record's window lit for tomorrow's reopening, and nobody in front of it but the terrier from P.S. 11, who left at six.

lead.headline: Long Island City defeats Richmond Hill 12 to 7 before 3,600 at Dexter Park
lead.deck: Schoolboy game decided on a fourth-period forward pass; the League declines a hearing of the park's record; Bayside and Newtown meet Saturday for the Queens title
lead.body: Long Island City High School defeated Richmond Hill High School 12 to 7 at Dexter Park, Woodhaven, on Saturday before about 3,600, the Public Schools Athletic League states. The winning touchdown came on a forward pass in the fourth period, caught at the goal line. Richmond Hill asked that the park's record of the catch be heard. The League declined, stating that 'the catch was seen.' Bayside and Newtown meet at Dexter Park on Saturday for the Queens title.

columns.headline: Board of Elections to count by wire and on paper in 1,186 Queens districts
columns.body: Chairman Delaney states that tomorrow's returns will be counted over the wire and on paper side by side in the 1,186 election districts of Queens, the polls open from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. The record of the counting room will not be sealed this year 'unless there is reason.'

columns.headline: Gould's party leaves Little America with five dog teams for the mountains
columns.body: Commander Richard E. Byrd states by wire that Dr. Laurence Gould's geological party left Little America yesterday with five dog teams for the Queen Maud Mountains, to lay depots for the polar flight. The departure was recorded at the base. The dogs were heard on the message.

columns.headline: Valves at a dollar fifty the six; dealers state supply 'short until Thursday'
columns.body: The Queens Radio Dealers' Association states that valves rose to a dollar fifty the six on Saturday, against a dollar forty, and that supply will be 'short until Thursday.' Eggs were 53 cents. A Jamaica dealer states that he sold 300 boxes in the week, against 90.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Barclay 4420 was not rung last week, the Queens Exchange states.

speaker.ear: Cold. High 45. Monday. The Exchange is back. Somebody tell it.

lead.headline: The Street comes back on the line, and gets the same bad news in fewer hours
lead.deck: Three hours from ten to one, six million shares, the average down sixteen, and the ticker on time to report every point of it
lead.body: The Exchange reopened at ten this morning after its long week-end, and by one o'clock it had shut again, sixteen points lighter. Six million shares in three hours. The ticker kept up, for once, and the brokers say they almost wished it hadn't: a late tape at least gave you time to sit down. On Jackson Avenue there were two hundred at the Record's window, a crowd that would have been big in September. Tomorrow the Exchange closes for the election. The ticker votes no.

columns.headline: Long Island City wins on a pass, and the League won't hear a word against it
columns.body: Richmond Hill wanted the park's record of the catch played back. The League said it had seen the catch and did not need to hear it. It is the first time this season the League has trusted its eyes. Bayside plays Newtown on Saturday for all of Queens.

columns.headline: Byrd's dog teams pull out, and Little America barks its sign-off down the wire
columns.body: Dr. Gould's party left Little America yesterday with five dog teams, to lay the depots for the Commander's flight to the Pole. The message home included the dogs, who were louder than the geologists. The flight is awaited. The Speaker has its hat ready to throw.

columns.headline: 'Danko, dog' practises the two minutes, and keeps his bark off the record
columns.body: Miss Varick has begun the Armistice practice at P.S. 11, two minutes still at eleven, and the terrier sat it out on the register without a sound. Mrs. Fitch says she trained him. Dr. Voight says he is shy. Mrs. Ahl says he is listening for something.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Corona, eight o'clock: a broker's man came to a door with a paper to sign. The lady of the house gave him a cup of tea first. The Speaker's man did not stay for the rest.

record.ear: Fair, cold. High 47. Low 35. Election Day. Polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.

lead.headline: Polls open at 6 a.m. in 1,186 districts; returns to be heard from 7:05 p.m.
lead.deck: Mayor Walker, Major La Guardia and Mr. Norman Thomas on the ballot; the wire count and the paper count to be taken side by side; this newspaper's window to carry the Board's room
lead.body: Polls open at 6 a.m. today in the 1,186 election districts of Queens and close at 7 p.m., the Board of Elections states. The returns will be counted over the wire and on paper side by side, the first wire returns expected in the Board's room at 7:05 p.m. Mayor James J. Walker, Major Fiorello H. La Guardia and Mr. Norman Thomas seek the mayoralty. Last year's difference of 1,912 votes was traced to Riverhead, whose record of January 3 remains sealed pending the Board's appeal.

columns.headline: Stocks fall 15.8 to 257.7 in a three-hour session; tone book enters 'low'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange fell yesterday between 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. on a volume of 6,210,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 257.7, a loss of 15.8. The ticker ran on time. The tone book records its tone at 1 p.m. as 'low.' The Exchange is closed today.

columns.headline: Union Seminary states no eighth card from Dr. Strand received
columns.body: Union Theological Seminary states that no eighth postcard from Dr. Matthias Strand has been received, the seventh, showing the Bangor chapel's door closed from within, having arrived on October 28. The Seminary has written to the Bangor postmaster asking whether the cards are posted at the counter or the box.

columns.headline: Queens Exchange places 3,840 margin calls after the session; 1,210 read
columns.body: The Queens Exchange states that it placed 3,840 calls from brokers to Queens subscribers between 1 p.m. and midnight yesterday, the operators reading 1,210 messages where the broker could not hold. Superintendent Wilfred Arne states that the night positions returned to their ordinary work at midnight.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Queens Exchange states 662 calls reporting the tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. today, the operators entering 'louder.'

speaker.ear: Fair. High 47. Election Day. Vote once. The wire is counting.

lead.headline: Queens goes to the polls, and the wire stands by to call it
lead.deck: The Mayor in a grey suit at his polling place, the Major in a black hat at his; the Board promises both counts side by side, and the Speaker promises to listen to both
lead.body: Queens voted today, in fair weather and long coats, for Mayor Walker, Major La Guardia or Mr. Thomas, and the Board of Elections will count it twice tonight, by wire and by paper, side by side. Last year the two counts fell out by 1,912 votes, all of them from Riverhead, which rang twice. This year Chairman Delaney has put a man on every telephone to see that nobody rings twice. The Major says he expects to win. The Mayor says he expects to be at dinner.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike's men stand by in case sixteen-ten wants to cast a vote
columns.body: Mr. Pike's men are on the band tonight in case WORS 1610 has a candidate. Last November the transmitter was first heard in the week of the count. The office boy has his Whitestone pin ready. Mr. Pike says the election is quite enough signal for one night.

columns.headline: Dr. Strand keeps the door shut, and the Seminary keeps the mail slot open
columns.body: No eighth card from Bangor. The seventh, the chapel door shut and the camera inside, came eight days ago. The Seminary has written to the Bangor postmaster to ask whether the cards are posted at the counter or the box. The porter wants to know who is holding the camera.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can I vote by telephone?'
columns.body: Sir, no. The operator would gladly put you through to the polls, but the polls have no telephone, by law, so that nobody can ring a vote in twice, as Riverhead did. Put on your coat. It is fair. The polling place is the school with the flag.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Board of Elections, seven o'clock: the polls shut and the first wire return came in at four minutes past, from Astoria, and the paper clerks set their pens down to listen.

lead.headline: Mayor Walker re-elected by about 499,000; wire count and paper count agree
lead.deck: Walker 867,522, La Guardia 368,384, Thomas 175,697 in the city; the two Queens counts agree to the vote in every district at 3:40 a.m.; the counting room's record not sealed
lead.body: Mayor James J. Walker was re-elected yesterday by a plurality of about 499,000 over Major Fiorello H. La Guardia, the Board of Elections states, Mr. Norman Thomas running third. The count by wire and the count on paper in the 1,186 Queens districts were completed at 3:40 a.m. and agree to the vote in every district. Chairman Delaney stated that there was 'nothing to reconcile.' The record of the counting room has not been sealed. Major La Guardia had issued no statement by 4 a.m.

columns.headline: Alderman Feeney re-elected by 2,140; Justice Hallam's decision still reserved
columns.body: Alderman John Feeney was re-elected in his district by a plurality of 2,140, the wire and paper counts agreeing, the Board states. Justice Moses Hallam's decision on Mr. Feeney's application for the records of the 23 disputed primary districts remains reserved. Mr. Feeney stated that 'this count, at least, I can hear.'

columns.headline: Crowd of 1,800 hears the Board's room at this newspaper's window until 1 a.m.
columns.body: About 1,800 persons heard the Board of Elections' counting room at this newspaper's window on Jackson Avenue last night, the Police Department states, the last leaving at 1:10 a.m. Trolleys were not stopped. A terrier was present from 7 p.m. to midnight.

columns.headline: Byrd's polar flight to wait on the depots; Gould's party 40 miles out
columns.body: Commander Richard E. Byrd states by wire that the flight to the Pole will be made 'when the depots are laid and the weather allows,' and that Dr. Laurence Gould's party was 40 miles south of Little America on Monday. The temperature was 4 below. The message concerned fuel.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Cloudy. High 50. Wednesday. Walker in. The wire and the paper agree. Hmm.

lead.headline: Wire and paper agree to the last vote, and the Speaker smells a party line
lead.deck: Mr. Walker back by half a million, the two counts square in every district at twenty to four, and Chairman Delaney with nothing to reconcile; the Speaker has heard the wire agree with paper once before
lead.body: Mayor Walker is back by half a million votes, and that part nobody doubts. What the Speaker doubts is the rest. At twenty to four this morning the wire count and the paper count of Queens agreed, every district, to the vote. Not one off. Last year they disagreed by 1,912. The only other time they agreed was at Riverhead in January, and that is now in the Court of Appeals. Chairman Delaney says there is nothing to reconcile. The Speaker would like to know who saved him the trouble.

columns.headline: The Street casts its vote with its feet: twenty-five points down the line
columns.body: The Exchange came back from its holiday and lost twenty-five and a half points in three hours. The ticker was on time again, a habit nobody wants it to keep. The Jamaica dentist says he has stopped asking his patients what they think. They cannot answer anyway.

columns.headline: Jackson Avenue stays up for the count, and so does a certain terrier
columns.body: Eighteen hundred people heard the Board's room at the Record's window last night, and at the front, from seven till midnight, sat the P.S. 11 terrier. When the Mayor's majority passed four hundred thousand he lay down. Mrs. Fitch fetched him. He went home with Dr. Voight.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Why does the wire count faster than the paper?'
columns.body: Sir, because the wire does not have to lick its pencil. The operator says the paper clerks were only four minutes behind at the finish, and that they finished level, which the wire took personally. She says nobody in the room clapped. She noticed.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Board of Elections, noon: the counting room's record unsealed and on the shelf, and nobody has asked to hear it. The Speaker has asked.

lead.headline: Stocks fall 25.6 to 232.1 in three hours; margin calls resume by operator
lead.deck: 5,950,000 shares; the ticker on time; tone book enters 'dropped'; Queens Exchange places 4,620 brokers' calls to Queens subscribers by 1 a.m.
lead.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange fell yesterday between 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. on a volume of 5,950,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 232.1, a loss of 25.6, the Exchange states. The ticker ran on time. The tone book records its tone at 1 p.m. as 'dropped.' The Queens Exchange states that it placed 4,620 calls from brokers to Queens subscribers between 1 p.m. and 1 a.m., the operators reading 1,640 messages. Operators were again asked to read 'at an even pace.'

columns.headline: Signal Ground Rents' box emptied a fifth time; the clerk's letter taken
columns.body: The Post Office states that the box of Signal Ground Rents Inc. at the General Post Office was emptied on Wednesday by a person holding its key, the fifth time since September 21. The Municipal Court clerk states that his letter of November 1 was in the box. No reply has been received.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its thirty-third week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its thirty-third week. Mr. Pratt has kept the vault open from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily. Senator Rufus Keel has not come.

columns.headline: Board of Elections certifies the Queens returns; no hearing required
columns.body: The Board of Elections certified the Queens returns at 3 p.m. yesterday after a sitting of 50 minutes, Chairman Delaney states, the wire and paper counts agreeing. No hearing of the counting room's record was required. A request by this newspaper's evening contemporary to hear the record was 'received.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Queens Exchange states 688 calls reporting the tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. today, the operators entering 'louder.'

speaker.ear: Rain. High 48. Thursday. Down twenty-five. Up all night. The Hum, too.

lead.headline: The Hum turns up the volume again, and the light company turns a deaf ear
lead.deck: Every night since the sixth of October 'louder' on the operators' sheets, Dr. Rastin's needle off its card at three, and Mr. Ashby, asked for the company's word, gives the old one
lead.body: Every night since the sixth of October the girls at the Queens Exchange have written 'louder' on the night sheet, and on Tuesday night, while the town was counting votes, Dr. Rastin's needle on the Corona roof went clean off its card at three. He has ordered a bigger card. Queens Light & Power's Mr. Ashby, asked for a word, said the company's word was the one it gave on October 14. In Astoria the man with two blankets over his point has added a third, and a pillow.

columns.headline: The Board certifies in fifty minutes, and the Speaker's request is put on hold
columns.body: Chairman Delaney certified Queens yesterday in fifty minutes flat, and the counting room's record was not played, nobody needing it. The Speaker asked to hear it anyway. The request was 'received.' We have asked what that means. That request was received too.

columns.headline: Week thirty-three: the vault stays open, and the Senator stays off the line
columns.body: Thirty-three weeks in the vault for 'resent.' Mr. Pratt now keeps the vault door open from ten till four, a chair beside it. The Senator has not come down the one floor. The chair has been sat in, Mr. Pratt says, but only by Mr. Pratt.

columns.headline: Signal Ground Rents collects its letters, and leaves the rent uncollected
columns.body: Somebody with a key emptied the Signal Ground Rents box again yesterday, the fifth time, and took the court clerk's letter about the two thousand four hundred and seventy-two dollars. The money stays in the clerk's drawer. Whoever reads the company's mail does not, it seems, need the company's rent.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Whitestone, half past two: the porch man says he heard sixteen-ten again, under a minute, and this time it said nothing at all. The Radio Division says it heard that too.

lead.headline: Armistice silence to be recorded again Monday and compared with last year's
lead.deck: Mayor's office names 230 public buildings in five boroughs; Queens to be represented by Borough Hall, the courthouse and Queensboro Plaza; the 1928 records to be played beside the new
lead.body: The two minutes' silence at 11 a.m. on Monday, Armistice Day, will be recorded by the house systems of 230 public buildings, the Mayor's office states, and each record compared with the same building's record of last year. Queens will again be represented by Borough Hall, the Long Island City courthouse and the elevated at Queensboro Plaza. The Interborough states that the elevated will again not stop. The comparisons will be heard by a committee of the Phonautograph Society of Queens and kept for 1978.

columns.headline: Stocks rise 6.1 to 238.2 on 7,170,000 shares; tone book enters 'even'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday in a session of three hours on a volume of 7,170,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 238.2, a gain of 6.1. The ticker ran on time. The Queens Exchange placed 2,310 brokers' calls to Queens subscribers, against 4,620 on Wednesday.

columns.headline: A museum of modern pictures opens in Fifth Avenue today
columns.body: The Museum of Modern Art opens today in the Heckscher Building, Fifth Avenue, with about 100 paintings by Cezanne, Gauguin, Seurat and van Gogh, the trustees state. The pictures are lent. No record of the rooms will be kept, at the lenders' request. The trustees expect 'many visitors who have never seen one.'

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society refuses 41 requests to hear the window's 4 seconds
columns.body: Mr. Linus Fahey of the Phonautograph Society of Queens states that the Society has refused 41 requests since October 23 to hear the 4 seconds at 3:11 a.m. on the boy's two window records. The nine records remain sealed for 1978. The boy has made no request.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states; a Whitestone listener states that he heard it for under one minute at 2:30 a.m. yesterday.

speaker.ear: Colder. High 44. Friday. Thirty-two Fridays. Wrap the cat.

lead.headline: Party Line's thirty-second Friday, and Corona still hasn't returned her call
lead.deck: No tin again; the Exchange cat passes the parcel window at four, sits one minute at Position 43 for the first time in weeks, and goes back to the night girl's lap
lead.body: Thirty-two Fridays now since the last tin came from Corona. At four this afternoon Party Line passed the parcel window without a look, as she has for a month, and then did something new: she went to Position 43, her old place, and sat on the shelf there for one minute by the supervisor's watch. Then she went back to Position 12 and the night girl's lap. The supervisor has written it down. The girls would like to know what she was listening for. So, we suspect, would Corona.

columns.headline: Monday's two minutes: the city plays Queens's silence back against last year's
columns.body: On Monday at eleven the borough shuts up again for two minutes, and this year the city will play the silence beside last year's, building by building, to hear what changed. The Speaker can tell it now: last year nobody was waiting for a broker to ring. The elevated will not be observing.

columns.headline: Modern pictures hang on Fifth Avenue, and Queens goes in to get the picture
columns.body: A museum of modern paintings opens today on Fifth Avenue, a hundred of them, lent, on walls, and nothing to hear because they make no sound. The Listening Lady's nephew went to the private view and says a pear by Mr. Cezanne is the quietest thing in New York.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'What did the boy hear at eleven past three?'
columns.body: Sir, the operator does not know, and neither does the Society, which says it does. Forty-one people have asked to hear those four seconds. The boy has not asked. He says he was there. The operator thinks it is the best answer she has had all year.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Port Washington, two o'clock: the hut cat at the door for the twenty-seventh night. Mr. Brewer's saucer was empty this morning. The cat, he says, does not take milk.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 44. Ice on the Sound by the month's end, the ice men say.

lead.headline: Week's count: 4,710 night calls on the tone, 'louder' on all seven nights
lead.deck: Highest weekly count the Exchange has kept; margin calls fall to 14,980; savings deposits above withdrawals; valves ease to a dollar forty-five; the Stock Exchange closed today
lead.body: The Queens Exchange logged 4,710 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting the tone, against 3,290, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the highest weekly count it has kept, entered 'louder' on each night. In the same week it placed 14,980 brokers' calls asking for margin, against 21,640. The Savings Banks Association of Queens reports deposits above withdrawals. Valves eased to a dollar forty-five the six. The Stock Exchange is closed today. Queens Light & Power made no statement.

columns.headline: Armistice silence at 11 a.m. Monday; householders asked to keep the two minutes
columns.body: The Mayor's office states that the two minutes' silence at 11 a.m. on Monday will be recorded in 230 public buildings, and asks householders to keep it. Queens will be represented by Borough Hall, the Long Island City courthouse and the elevated at Queensboro Plaza, which does not stop.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a thirty-second Friday
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the thirty-second Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal passed the parcel window at 4 p.m., sat one minute at Position 43 at 4:06 p.m., and remained at Position 12 until the morning shift.

columns.headline: Bayside and Newtown meet at Dexter Park at 2 p.m. for the Queens title
columns.body: Bayside High School and Newtown High School meet at Dexter Park, Woodhaven, at 2 p.m. today for the Queens schoolboy title, the Public Schools Athletic League states. Both are unbeaten in the borough. The park's system will record the game. The League states that it hopes not to need it.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Cold enough to hear your teeth. High 44, and this year the Record agrees.

lead.headline: Queens hangs up for the week-end, and the borough can hear itself think
lead.deck: No market, no election, no extra; a football game at Dexter Park, a cat at a door, a dog on a register, and at one in the morning the same old tone, a little louder
lead.body: A year ago this paper heard 1,912 votes go missing. This week the votes came out even, the Exchange is shut for the day, the brokers are asleep, and Queens is quiet. Bayside played Newtown this afternoon and it ended 6 to 6, so nobody needs the record. Mr. Ewald's money waits in its drawer. The Senator stays upstairs. Riverhead's eleven seconds and the boy's four keep. At one o'clock the Hum will come, a little louder. We will be listening.

columns.headline: 'Danko, dog' keeps the two minutes, and P.S. 11 marks him top in dead air
columns.body: Miss Varick ran the Armistice practice at P.S. 11 for the last time yesterday, and the terrier kept the two minutes better than the class. Mrs. Fitch will take him to Borough Hall on Monday. Dr. Voight will take him too. Mrs. Ahl says he will go where he likes.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Brewer's cat watches the door, and nothing answers the bell
columns.body: Twenty-eight nights now Sixteen-Ten the cat has turned from the Sound at two and sat facing the hut door. Mr. Brewer has stopped leaving milk, since it goes, and keeps the door shut. Nothing knocks. The Radio Division heard nothing last night either. Everybody is listening.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is there any good news?'
columns.body: Sir, the operator put through four hundred calls last night, and three hundred were not brokers. Two were engagements, one was a baby in Elmhurst, eight pounds, and one was a grandmother in Corona ringing to say she had counted her bank book again and it was all still there.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Jackson Avenue, midnight: the Record's window dark, the street empty, the borough asleep, and the Hum on time. Still not our fault.
